content: Atorvastatin is a medication prescribed to reduce cholesterol and other fatty substances in the blood. It is used in conjunction with lifestyle changes such as a healthy diet, weight loss, and regular exercise. Atorvastatin belongs to a class of drugs known as HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, or statins. It works by slowing the production of cholesterol in the body. Excess cholesterol and fats can accumulate along the walls of blood vessels, a condition called atherosclerosis, which reduces blood flow and oxygen supply to the heart, brain, and other parts of the body. Lowering cholesterol levels can help reduce the risk of heart disease, angina (chest pain), strokes, and heart attacks. Atorvastatin is available as an oral tablet and is typically taken once daily, with or without food. It is important to take it at the same time each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not take more or less of the medication than prescribed. Your doctor may start you on a low dose and gradually increase it every 2-4 weeks. Continue taking atorvastatin even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before taking atorvastatin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to it or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription drugs, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take. Certain medications, such as antibiotics (e.g., erythromycin), oral contraceptives, other cholesterol-lowering drugs (e.g., fenofibrate, gemfibrozil, niacin), and spironolactone, may interact with atorvastatin. Your doctor may need to adjust your doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have liver disease, consume large amounts of alcohol, or have a history of liver disease. Atorvastatin should not be taken during pregnancy or while breastfeeding, as it may harm the fetus or infant. If you become pregnant while taking atorvastatin, stop the medication and contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking atorvastatin. Discuss the safe use of alcohol with your doctor, as alcohol can increase the risk of serious side effects. Follow a low-cholesterol, low-fat diet while taking atorvastatin. This includes foods like cottage cheese, fat-free milk, fish (not canned in oil), vegetables, poultry, egg whites, and polyunsaturated oils (e.g., corn, safflower, canola, soybean). Avoid high-fat foods such as fatty meats, egg yolks, whole milk, cream, butter, pastries, fried foods, and certain oils (e.g., coconut, palm). Consult your doctor about consuming grapefruit juice, as it may interact with the medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Atorvastatin may cause side effects. Common minor side effects include diarrhea, headache, difficulty sleeping, dizziness, joint pain, sore throat, and upper respiratory infections. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, though rare, require immediate medical attention. These include muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness; lack of energy; fever; chest pain; swelling of the hands, feet, or lower legs; nausea; extreme fatigue; unusual bleeding or bruising; loss of appetite; pain in the upper right abdomen; flu-like symptoms; yellowing of the skin or eyes; rash; hives; itching; difficulty breathing or swallowing; swelling of the face, throat, tongue, or extremities; hoarseness; pain during urination; or frequent urination. If you experience any unusual problems while taking atorvastatin, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store atorvastatin in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order tests before and during treatment to monitor your response to atorvastatin. Inform laboratory personnel that you are taking this medication before undergoing any tests. Do not share your medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
